# Job Chapter 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 422v

---

**18:1** And-answered Bildad the-Shuchite [Shuhite] and-said:

**18:2** "Until when [ad anah] will-you-set [tesimu] traps [qintsei] for-words [lemillin]? Consider [tavinu], and-after [achar] we-will-speak [nedabber]. **18:3** Why are-we-counted [necheshavnu] as-beasts [kabehemah], [and] are-stupid [nitamnu] in-your-eyes [be'einekhem]?

**18:4** [O one who] tears [toref] his-soul [nafsho] in-his-anger [be-appo] — for-your-sake [lema'anekha] will-the-earth [erets] be-forsaken [te'azev]? And-will-a-rock [tsur] be-moved [ye'teq] from-its-place [mimqomo]?

**18:5** Indeed [gam] the-light [or] of-the-wicked [reshaim] will-be-extinguished [yid'akh], and-the-flame [sheviv] of-his-fire [ishho] will-not shine [lo yiggah]. **18:6** The-light [or] grows-dark [chashakh] in-his-tent [be-aholo], and-his-lamp [nero] above-him is-extinguished [yid'akh].

**18:7** His-strong steps [tsa'adei ono] are-shortened [yetsaru], and-his-own-counsel [atsato] casts-him-down [tashlikhehu]. **18:8** For he-is-cast [shullach] into-a-net [bereshhet] by-his-own-feet [beraglov], and-upon a-snare [sebakhah] he-walks [yithalekh].

**18:9** A-trap [pach] seizes [yochaz] [his] heel [be-aqev]; a-snare [tsammim] takes-hold [yachazek] of-him. **18:10** Hidden [tamun] in-the-ground [ba-arets] [is] his-cord [chavlo], and-his-trap [umalkudeto] upon the-path [alei nativ].

**18:11** All-around [saviv] terrors [ballahot] frighten-him [bi'atuhu], and-scatter-him [vahefitsuhu] at-his-feet [leraglov]. **18:12** His-strength [ono] is-hunger-bitten [yehi ra'ev], and-calamity [eid] is-ready [nakhon] at-his-side [letsalo].

**18:13** It-devours [yo'khal] the-limbs [baddei] of-his-skin [oro]; the-firstborn of-death [bekhor maveth] devours his-limbs [baddav]. **18:14** He-is-torn [yinnateq] from-his-tent [me-aholo], his-security [mivtacho], and-it-marches-him [vetatsi'dehu] to-the-king of-terrors [le-melekh ballahot].

**18:15** It-dwells [tishkon] in-his-tent [be-aholo] that-which-is-not-his [mibbeeli lo]; brimstone [gofrit] is-scattered [yezoreh] upon his-habitation [naveh]. **18:16** From-beneath [mittachat] his-roots [sharashav] dry-up [yiveshu], and-from-above [mimma'al] his-branch [qetsiro] withers [yimmal].

**18:17** His-memory [zikhro] perishes [avad] from-the-earth [min erets], and-no name [shem] [belongs] to-him on-the-face of-the-street [chuts]. **18:18** They-thrust-him [yehdefuhu] from-light [me-or] into-darkness [el choshekh], and-from the-world [tevel] they-chase-him [yenidduhu].

**18:19** No offspring [lo nin] and-no posterity [lo nekhed] [has he] among-his-people [be'ammo], and-no survivor [sarid] in-his-dwelling-places [bimegurav]. **18:20** Over-his-day [al yomo] the-west [acharonim] is-appalled [nashammu], and-the-east [qadmonim] is-seized [achazu] [with] horror [sa'ar].

**18:21** Surely [akh] these [are] the-dwellings [mishkenot] of-the-unrighteous [avval], and-this [is] the-place [meqom] of-the-one-who-does-not-know [lo yada] God [el]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.13 — "the firstborn of death":** Hebrew *bekhor maveth* — a personification of disease as Death's eldest son. This chilling image suggests that the most terrible diseases are Death's own offspring, sent ahead to devour the wicked.

**v.14 — "the king of terrors":** Hebrew *melekh ballahot* — Death personified as a king who rules over all terrors. The wicked man is marched before this king as a prisoner. The phrase has become a permanent part of English idiom.

**v.5-6 — Lamp and light imagery:** Bildad employs the "lamp" metaphor throughout — the lamp of the wicked goes out, the light in his tent darkens. In the ancient Near East, the extinguishing of a household lamp symbolized the end of a family line.

**v.19 — "no offspring, no posterity":** The Hebrew uses two terms — *nin* (offspring) and *nekhed* (posterity/grandchild) — covering both immediate descendants and future generations. Total annihilation of the family line.

*— EMET*
